scope: Proposition 3.6 (Stopped cell expansion and positive domination) of the manuscript “The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals” (preprints/The-Boltzmann-Grad-limit-for-stable-radial-potentials-on-regular-kinetic-intervals-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For k > |R|, the finite-cloud expansion equals its complete diagrams with fewer than k selected labels plus a finite signed remainder. Each remainder term is of one of the following types. 1. Its root group A already has |A| ≥ k. Its transport is cR I (A)HI R,A times the factor ΞI({A}; S \A) ∈ [0, 1]. 2. Its completed generations and its final partial generation select a union U with |U| ≥ k. Im- mediately before the last selected component B∗, the number of selected labels is less than k. All displayed groups satisfy the connectivity, initial-polymer, same-generation avoidance, and preceding-generation touch conditions of Definition 3.1. Its weight is the corresponding sign and indicators times a factor ϑI of the form (3.15), lying in [0, 1]. In the second case the overshoot is by at most one additional component. In particular, if every component of every trial subsystem formed from initial polymers has size at most D, then |A| ≤ |R|D, and a stopped union has size at most max{|R|D, k − 1 + D}. Replacing the sign by +1 and dropping the last factor gives a pointwise positive domination of the total variation of the remainder. Its expected version is a sum of these positive contact expressions integrated against the initial isolated factorial measures of the selected unions, with the factors µm/m! of (3.11). This is an identity and a domination statement, not a claim that this sum tends to zero.
